children: Thai stocks are likely to continue facing some profit-taking following its ascent earlier this year, UOB Kay Hian analysts say in a note. The benchmark SET Index has declined 1.8% in August, mainly due to profit-taking, particularly in the electronics sector. The Thai stock market has no near-term catalysts, while investors are concerned over external headwinds, including the Fed's potential rate increases. However, any pullback in Thai equities are likely to be contained, they say. The market is being supported by capital inflows from the domestic bond market, they add. The SET Index is 0.5% higher at 1584.25.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
